newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH says yen rise since April positive.
newsitem.headline: LVMH says yen rise since April positive.

text.p: Luxury goods group LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton said on Thursday that if a recovery seen in the yen since April takes hold, it would be positive for the group.
"The yen, which was weak until April, has steadied very recently relative to the dollar," LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault told the annual shareholders' meeting.

"If this trend is confirmed, it would have a favourable impact on the rest of the year. Further, the firmness in the dollar and sterling are favourable factors, as is the continued economic growth in the United States," he said.
Arnault declined to give a results forecast for the group.
LVMH said in March when it reported its 1996 results that its objective was to show a rise in results and turnover in 1997 excluding the impact of the acquisition of Duty Free Shoppers.

Its 1996 profit fell to 3.68 billion francs ($640.1 million) from 4.05 billion in 1995 after it reported a capital loss on the sale of a third of its stake in Guinness Plc to help pay for the $2.6 billion acquisition of San Francisco-based DFS.

Arnault said the yen's weakness had been unfavourable for DFS's Japanese clients. Coupled with DFS's investment plans, "the two elements risk weighing momentarily on the profitability of DFS's activities. Nonetheless, DFS's contribution to LVMH's net pre-exceptional result will be positive in 1997," he said.
LVMH said in January that the DFS acquisition would have a positive impact on cashflow and pre-exceptional profit before goodwill amortisation but weigh on earnings per share.
